question: Is among-radiation variation in hierarchical hidden fine-state memory simply an extension of how long exact fine flower-colour states persist across relative evolutionary divergence?

analysis_frame.source_hash_contract: same frozen final_dataset.csv and trees.zip hashes used by both existing analyses
analysis_frame.included_units: intersection of the 21 existing hidden-memory opportunity clades and completed relative-time half-depth clades

primary_hypothesis.test: Spearman rho with 99999 two-sided label permutations
primary_hypothesis.rationale: If hidden memory primarily reflects unusually persistent exact fine states, clades with longer relative fine-state half-depth should show stronger within-coarse hidden-memory effects.

secondary_descriptive: fine pseudo-loglik gain over frequency-only q versus hidden-memory effect
fine minus coarse half-depth versus hidden-memory effect
secondary_rule: Secondary relations are descriptive only and cannot rescue a failed primary hypothesis.
interpretation_if_supported: Hidden-memory realization covaries with the relative persistence duration of exact fine colour states, linking nested state organization to a temporal persistence axis.
interpretation_if_not_supported: Hierarchical hidden memory is not reducible to longer relative persistence of exact fine colour states; temporal persistence and within-coarse organization remain separable evolutionary axes.
boundaries: post-outcome exploratory because both component outcomes already exist
relative divergence depth only; no absolute-time claim in Ma
shared source/tree information must be disclosed
no ecological or molecular cause inferred
secondary relations cannot replace the primary test
